subject: math.OC
name: Strongly polynomial linear programming
statement: Is there an algorithm for rational linear programming using a number of arithmetic operations polynomial only in the numbers of variables and constraints, with all intermediate bit lengths polynomial in the input encoding length?
importance: It is a central unresolved complexity question for convex optimization.
status_note: Polynomial-time algorithms depending on coefficient bit length are established; removing that dependence from the arithmetic operation count is the open target.

references.title: Smale, Mathematical problems for the next century, Problem 9

subject: math.OC
name: Polynomial Hirsch conjecture
statement: Is the diameter of the vertex-edge graph of every d-dimensional polytope with m facets bounded by a polynomial in d and m?
importance: It asks whether polyhedral optimization always has short edge paths at the level of combinatorial geometry.
status_note: The original linear Hirsch bound is false. This asks about ordinary edge diameter, not the circuit-diameter variant addressed by recent results.

references.title: Diameters of Cocircuit Graphs of Oriented Matroids: An Update
Circuit Diameter of Polyhedra is Strongly Polynomial

subject: math.OC
name: Polynomial-time P-matrix linear complementarity
statement: Given a rational P-matrix M (all principal minors positive) and rational q, can the unique solution of w=Mz+q, w≥0, z≥0, wᵀz=0 be found in polynomial time?
importance: It is a basic unresolved algorithmic problem for equilibrium models and complementarity optimization.
status_note: The solution exists uniquely under the P-matrix promise; polynomial algorithms for restricted matrix classes do not settle the general promised problem.

references.title: Foniok et al., Pivoting in Linear Complementarity: Two Polynomial-Time Cases

subject: math.OC
name: Polynomial-time solution of parity games
statement: For a finite directed graph with every vertex having an outgoing edge, vertices assigned to two players, and nonnegative integer priorities, can the winner of the infinite-play game be decided in polynomial time, where the largest priority visited infinitely often determines the winner by its parity?
importance: It is a central algorithmic problem for adversarial control, program verification, and infinite-horizon games.
status_note: Memoryless winning strategies exist, and quasipolynomial algorithms are known. Polynomial time in the graph size and number of distinct priorities remains open.

references.title: Calude et al., Deciding parity games in quasipolynomial time

subject: math.OC
name: P versus NP for combinatorial optimization
statement: Does there exist a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given a Boolean formula in 3-CNF, decides whether some truth assignment satisfies all clauses?
importance: Its resolution would determine whether efficiently verifiable solutions can always be found efficiently.
status_note: This NP-complete decision problem has a polynomial algorithm exactly when P=NP; neither direction is proved.

references.title: Clay Mathematics Institute, P versus NP

subject: math.OC
name: NP certificates for semidefinite feasibility
statement: For rational symmetric matrices A₀,…,A_m, does deciding whether some real x satisfies A₀+ΣxᵢAᵢ ⪰ 0 belong to NP in the binary Turing model?
importance: It addresses the exact computational foundations of semidefinite optimization.
status_note: Approximate feasible optimization with regularity promises has polynomial algorithms. Exact feasibility can require irrational solutions and is not thereby known to have polynomial-size certificates.

references.title: Ramana, An exact duality theory for semidefinite programming and its complexity implications

subject: math.OC
name: Exact optimum of Witsenhausen’s counterexample
statement: Let X∼N(0,25), V∼N(0,1) independently, U=f(X), Y=X+U+V, and Z=X+U−g(Y). Determine the globally optimal measurable strategies f,g and exact infimum of E[0.04U²+Z²] among finite-cost strategies.
importance: It is the canonical unsolved nonlinear decentralized control problem and shows why linear Gaussian control intuition can fail.
status_note: Nonlinear policies outperform the best linear policies; existence, bounds, and numerical candidates do not characterize the exact global optimum.

subject: math.OC
name: Small-time global boundary control with no-slip walls
statement: For the two-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equation in a rectangle, can every smooth compatible divergence-free initial velocity be driven exactly to rest in every prescribed time T>0 using only boundary controls on the two vertical sides, while keeping zero velocity on the horizontal walls and applying no distributed force?
importance: It asks whether viscous flows can be stopped arbitrarily quickly through limited boundary access.
status_note: Navier-slip variants and results using a small distributed phantom force are known; the force-free problem with uncontrolled no-slip walls is the scope here.

references.title: Coron, Marbach and Sueur, Controllability of the Navier–Stokes Equation in a Rectangle with a Little Help of a Distributed Phantom Force

subject: math.OC
name: Four-thirds integrality-gap conjecture for metric TSP
statement: For every finite complete graph with nonnegative metric edge costs, is the minimum traveling-salesman tour cost at most 4/3 times the optimum of the subtour-elimination linear program: x≥0, Σ_{e incident to v}x_e=2 for each vertex, and Σ_{e crossing S}x_e≥2 for every nonempty proper vertex subset S?
importance: It asks for the exact strength of the standard linear relaxation for one of the central combinatorial optimization problems.
status_note: Examples approach the lower bound 4/3. General upper bounds and improved approximation algorithms still leave a gap; the conjecture concerns this specific relaxation.

references.title: Karlin, Klein and Oveis Gharan, A (Slightly) Improved Approximation Algorithm for Metric TSP

subject: math.OC
name: Square-root-sum problem in NP
statement: Given positive integers a₁,…,a_n and an integer b in binary, does deciding whether Σ√aᵢ ≤ b belong to NP?
importance: This arithmetic comparison problem underlies exact certification of Euclidean optimization costs.
status_note: The problem is decidable and lies in PSPACE; known algorithms do not establish polynomial-size NP certificates in general.

references.title: Allender et al., On the Complexity of Numerical Analysis
